A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OPTIMIST research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original recall, latency, and prediction-error experiments on six datasets, with parameter and clustering analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in Section 3 and its experimental appendices.

M1.justification: The optimistic estimator, Chebyshev-based score, masked covariance sketch, and Algorithm 1 are retained. The general solution moves from v2 Appendix A to v4 Section 2.2; faster eigensolvers are discussed as possible implementations, without establishing an implemented method change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Text2Image, Music, DeepImage, GloVe, MSMarco-MiniLM, and NQ-Ada2. The represented tasks, cosine-to-inner-product normalization, clustering alternatives, and SSD/blob-storage scenarios remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The comparator roster remains Mean, NormalizedMean, SCANN, and SUBPARTITION; KRT is newly identified with SUBPARTITION. However, Section 3.1 in both versions specifies maximum-score aggregation, while v4 Appendix B calls the statistic 'the mean of the sub-shards.' This conflict leaves any actual revision to the evaluated baseline unresolved.

E3.justification: Dataset and query sizes, fixed partitions, exact-search recall evaluation, default hyperparameters, and normalization are retained. Latency experiments retain the PQ configuration, AWS hardware, storage types, and one-, two-, and four-thread settings. No additional evaluation design is established.

E4.justification: The sketch-rank and optimism sweeps, alternative-clustering comparisons, eigenvalue histograms, thread comparisons, and prediction-error analyses are retained. Their redistribution into v4 Appendices C and E–J does not add or remove substantive analyses.

E5.justification: Unlike v2, v4 checklist item 7 claims that OPTIMIST's improvements are statistically significant, often with p-values below 0.001. This adds significance reporting, but supplies no test procedure, run counts, seeds, or confidence intervals and does not establish additional runs.

E6.justification: v4 adds the aggregate significance finding and reports NQ-Ada2 top-10 recall under spherical KMeans in Figure 8(a). That panel reuses v2 Figure 10(a)'s standard-KMeans plot, so new measurements are not established. Existing benchmark values and plotted curves match; Table 3 consolidates earlier results with rounding.

T1.justification: v4 Section 2.3.3 adds construction-time analysis, contrasting O(n d^2 + d^3) computation with an O(n d log(d) t) randomized Block Krylov implementation. The central definitions, lemmas, and appendix proofs remain substantively unchanged; the general moment-based derivation is relocated.

C1.justification: The principal contributions remain optimistic moment-based routing, a compact covariance sketch, and comparable recall with up to approximately 50% fewer probes. Explicit mentions of cosine similarity and independence from clustering clarify capabilities already present in v2.

C2.justification: v4 replaces v2's 'best upper-bound' characterization with an explicit discussion of looseness and the unresolved approximation gap without distributional assumptions. Section 3.2 also newly interprets reduced point probing as a reasonable latency proxy. Existing hardware-dependent benefits and DeepImage limitations remain.

D1.justification: v4 Appendix D adds dataset and embedding-model license information, including missing license information for Music. Checklist item 5 newly documents processed-data links available through the repository. Both versions already provide the Rust implementation description and the same code-repository address.

R1.justification: The new Appendix B substantially expands research positioning: it distinguishes supervised routing and learned partitioning from unsupervised routing, justifies excluding supervised comparisons, explains SCANN's routing role, and connects SUBPARTITION to KRT/HRT. New citations also support the computational-complexity discussion.

P1.justification: The main narrative is extensively condensed and reorganized. The general solution moves into the main text, while dataset descriptions and parameter analyses move to dedicated appendices. Experimental supplements are reorganized by topic, and related work and a NeurIPS checklist are added.

P2.justification: The ACM layout becomes a NeurIPS layout. Tables 1 and 2 are placed side by side, Table 2 is transposed, and summary Table 3 is added. Numerous existing plot panels are regrouped or relocated, and the latency grid is transposed, while the plotted curves themselves are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves assessment and reuse through computational-complexity analysis, fuller research positioning, clearer bound qualifications, and license and processed-data access documentation. These benefits are limited by the conflicting SUBPARTITION descriptions and significance claims without test details. The revision improves documentation more clearly than it strengthens empirical validation.
